name: WU_crystallization_protocol_1
text: Default Washington University crystallization setup:  Purified proteins are exchanged into crystallization buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 25 mM NaCl) using a separate Amicon Ultra centrifugal filtration device of the appropriate MWCO for each protein. The centrifugation is continued until the final protein concentration reaches between 10-20 mg/ml.  Place 2ul of the sample into the NanoVue spectrophotometer (GE-Healthcare) to obtain an OD. The approximate concentration can obtained for each protein from its OD using the proteins theoretical extinction coefficient calculated by ProtParam (Expasy website). The concentration process is monitored closely for signs of precipitation to prevent exceeding sample solubility.  Depending on the particular protein, 2mM DDT may be added to inhibit protein cross-linking by disulfide bond formation between surface-exposed cysteine.  Crystallization trials are carried out in 96 well MRC 2 plates  (Hampton Research Cat# HR3-083) by sitting-drop vapor-diffusion technique.  Each well is filled with 50 ul of commercially available 96 well crystallization screens (JCSG, PEGs, Index, Cryo, et cetera) by hand using a multichannel pipette.  The crystallization drops are setup using a Mosquito nano-liter high throughput liquid handling robot (TTP labtech). Typically 0.3 ul protein and 0.3 ul well solution are combined for each drop. The plates are sealed with UV-transparent ClearSeal Film (Hampton Research Cat# HR4-521).  Each plate must contain a 4 digit WU-ID number, the date, the experimenters name, the proteins name, the screen name, and type of protein (native or SeMet).   The information for each plate must be entered into CrystalTrak software, a barcode printed, and an appropriate observation schedule chosen before placing the plate into the Gallery 700 side of the Minstrel-HT (Rigaku). INTRODUCTION Protocols provided for PepcDB represent the typical practices followed by the JCSG in the setup of proteins for crystallization trials.Individual details may vary for any particular target. JCSG proteins are typically expressed, purified, and then set up with 384 standard crystallization conditions derived from commercial sparse-matrix screens (Page et. al., 2003). This SOP describes the JCSG coarse screen (CS) plate setup process, from the receipt of purified proteins through image scheduling and the removal of expired plates. name: GNF Crystallization Protocol 2(fine screening)
text: JCSG FINE SCREEN PLATE SETUPS D. Carlton, T. Clayton, J. Paulsen October, 2007 1. INTRODUCTION Protocols provided for PepcDB represent the typical practices followed by the JCSG in the setup of proteins for crystallization trials.Individual details may vary for any particular target. This SOP describes the fine screen design and plate setup process, which follows the fine screen selection process. The goal of JCSG fine screen setups is to increase the number of quality crystals in order to facilitate target structure solution. This is accomplished by replicating and/or expanding on previous crystallization conditions. Three fine screen plate formats are typically employed, alone or in parallel, for a selected target: fine screen (FS), fine screen of a fine screen (FS-FS), and harvest plate (HP). JCSG FS and FS-FS plates explore conditions around crystallization leads by controlled variation of screen parameters, such as buffers, pH, temperature, precipitants, detergents, ligands, cofactors, and protein concentration. In contrast, JCSG HPs replicate a single screening condition multiple times. Each of three plate formats shares similar pathways: sample preparation, screen design, screen creation, fine screen setup, incubation, and imaging. 2. REFERENCES 2.1. Michael DiDonato, Ashley M. name: typical crystallization protocol at Wladek Minor group
text: Targets are first screened in commercially available crystallization screens, usually Hampton Research's Crystal Screen I and PEG/Ion screens, using hanging-drop vapor diffusion, usually in Nextal 24-well crystallization plates. Promising hits from the initial screens are optimized by grid variation of various crystallization parameters. Microseeding is also attempted where applicable. When proteins produce crystalline hits, Se-Met derivatives of the target are produced. The Se derivatives are also screened in the commercial screens and hits from the native optimization are repeated.

name: Reversibility of crystallization
text: Table of content: 1. Introduction 2. Materials 3. Instructions 4. Reference   1.0 Introduction This test allows fast identification of conditions leading to reversible precipitation, which are then selected for further screening fine screening.Conditions showing irreversible precipitation are excluded from further screening.  The set-up is provided by Rigaku using the automated Phoenix crystallization robot. The setup includes a new short program that allows the robot to remove solution from the reservoir wells prior to dilution of the reservoirs with water. No hardware changes are required on the standard setup of the robot to preform  the experiments. This protocol is suitable and can be applied to all crystallization experiments using  96 well sitting drop crystallization plates. It is most suitable to be used on all plates that show amorphous precipitate to identify which conditions lead to reversible precipitation. These conditions can then selected for fine screening of crystallization conditions. It also allows for fast exclusion of conditions  leading to a destabilization/denaturation of the protein as indicated by irreversible precipitation. 2.0 Materials 96 Well Crystallization Plates (any sitting drop 96 well plate that can be used that is compatible with the use in        the  Phoenix Crystallization Robot ! In areas with low humidity it is recommended to use 96 well plates with deep wells for the protein, as it reduces the evaporation rate of the drops) UV and IR transparent foil for re-sealing of the 96 well plates deep well block with dionized water Rigaku/Art Robinson Phoenix crystallization robot 3.0 Instructions 3.1 Sample preparation This experiment is done with plates where crystallization experiments have been performed in standard 96 well crystallization plates. The procedure can be done at any time after initial setup of the crystallization experiments. The optimal  time depends on the stability of the protein, i.e. the test of reversibility s

General crystallization protocol overview  Below are the most important steps to carrier out the crystallization of any protein in brief (Elaborate protocol will be updated). In any crystallization experiment the concentration of the protein should be at least 10 mg/mL. We use Hampton research kits for optimization.  Step 1: Make initial screens to identify pobeta-ible crystallization conditions. For this step we will use:  1. The vapor diffusion technique using the sitting drop method in plates of 96 wells. 2. Different crystallization kits from Hampton Research company. 3. The Phoenix Robot. 4. These experiments will be performed at 20 C  Step 2: As soon as the first microcrystals or microcrystalline precipitate are observed systematic optimization of the crystallization conditions in combination with seeding techniques will be used to growth of well ordered single crystals for structure determination.  In this case we will use the vapor diffusion technique using the hanging drop method in plates of 24 wells and will check different parameters such as:  1. Temperature 2. pH 3. Precipitant concentration 4. Use of different additives

General crystallization protocol overview (LCP method) Below are the steps to carry out LCP crystallization of any protein in brief. In any LCP experiment the concentration of the protein should be approximately 10 mg/mL. Step 1: Make initial screens to identify pobeta-ible crystallization conditions. For initial screening we use crystallisation kits from Hampton Research company. Screens are stored at 4 oC until use.  Step 2: Make cubic phase. 1. Load protein and monoolein (the default hosting lipid) at the ratio of 2 : 3 (w:w) in two separate syringes at room temperature. 2. Gently mix until a transparent cubic phase is achieved. 3. Leave the uniform cubic phase inside one syringe and transfer it onto any type of LCP robot. We use the SIAS robot. Step 3: Set up 96-well crystallisation plate by SIAS robot with 50 nL of cubic phase covered by 800 nL of precipitant solution. As soon as the first microcrystals or microcrystalline precipitates are observed systematic optimization of the crystallisation conditions will be used to grow well ordered single crystals for structure determination. We use the same crystallization method for this step too.  We vary the following parameters for optimization purpose: 1. Temperature 2. pH 3. Precipitant concentration 4. Use of different additives 5. Hosting lipids 6. Protein concentration

It is a method for determining whether a given precipitate is nanocrystalline or whether it is amorphous precipitate.  Using Second Harmonic Generation SONICC can determine the difference between crystalline and amorphous precipitate using a 1064nm femtosecond laser which when it hits a crystal two photon excites to 532nm.  This instrument is also equipped to perform UV-TPEF using the same laser with the photons being doubled twice once by a crystal in-system, and once by the protein, thus providing another signature to ensure that what is being visualized is protein crystals and not salt crystals. The set-up is provided Formulatrix. A detained description of the HTS Lab and its services can be found at http://www.hwi.buffalo.edu/faculty_research/crystallization.html  Materials list:  1.  Apogent Discoveries/Robbins Scientific Tango liquid handling system 2.  1536-well microassay plates 3.  Stock solutions of the 1536 chemical cocktails to be used as potential precipitants. text: PLI LCP Crystallization  Materials:  Emerald LCP Kit SKU:EB-LCPKIT 96-Well sitting drop crystallization plate  Method:  1) Heat host lipid at 42C 2) Cool lipid briefly 3) Pipette molten lipid into the back end of a Hamilton gastight syringe.  Insert the plunger into the syringe and expel any remaining air from the syringe. 4) Note the volume of molten lipid 5) Aspirate water using another Hamilton syringe.  The final ratio between the host lipid and water should be 60%:40% v/v. 6) Attach the syringe to a ratcheting dispenser. 7) Dispense LCP onto a 96-well plate. 8) Add 1uL of protein solution to each LCP bolus. 9) Cover the plate and incubate at 22C for 3 hours, allowing the protein to partition into the LCP. 10)  Uncover plate and add 1uL of crystallant from a screen to each well. 11)  Cover plate and observe every 2 days for 3 weeks.   PLI is described in the following peer reviewed article: Wallace E, Dranow D, Laible PD, Christensen J, Nollert P. Monoolein lipid phases as incorporation and enrichment materials for membrane protein crystallization. PLoS One. 2011;6(8):e24488. Epub 2011 Aug 3

name: crystallization
text: LCP Crystallization Protocol Materials: Emerald LCP Kit SKU:EB-LCPKIT LCP Sandwich Set SKU HR3-151 Method: 1) Aspirate target protein using a 100uL Hamilton syringe.  Record total volume. 2) Warm host lipid until molten 3) Remove lipid from heat and allow to cool briefly 4) Pipette enough lipid so that the lipid:protein ratio is 60% : 40% v/v into the back end of a Hamilton syringe with the plunger removed.  Expel lipid from the syringe until the correct volume is attained. 5) Attach the two Hamilton syringes via a syringe coupler 6) Pass the contents of the syringes through the syringe mixer at a rate of 1 pass every 2 seconds for 200 seconds, or until the lipid:protein mix is optically clear. 7) The LCP is now formed, and ready to dispense into a 96-well tray.  Attach the syringe containing the LCP to a ratcheting dispenser. 8) Direct the stream of a humidifier over a 96-well LCP sandwich plate. 9) Begin dispensing the LCP into each well of the sandwich plate 10) Overlay 1uL of crystallant solution on top of the LCP bolus. 11) Attach the cover slip to the adhesive seal, sealing the wells. 12) Use a plastic spreader to ensure each well is sealed. 13) Place the plate in a warm 20-22C incubator and observe every 48 hours using polarized light microscopy and UV fluorescence.

Molecular Dimension JCSG-plus 96 condition screen 4. Microscope for crystallization tray visualization 5. Corning 96-well crystallization plates Methods:  Crystallization screen protocol:  1. Bring crystallization cocktail solutions to room temperature. 2. Using a multichannel pipette, load 70 ul of the crystallization cocktail into the well reservoir. 3. Dispense 1.0 ul of membrane protein into the sample well. 4. Then dispense 1.0 ul of cocktail from the corresponding well reservoir into sample well. No additional mixing. 5. Store in 20C and/or 4C incubator. 6. Check crystallization plates immediately after plate is setup, then daily for one week and weekly for 3 additional weeks.

text: NESG high-throughput crystallization protocol July 2009  Targets selected for SeMet labeling ( decision based upon bioinformatic properties such as predicted probability of crystallizing and 1 or more internal Methionine's per 150 aa ), are sent to HAUPTMAN-WOODWARD INSTITUTE (http://www.hwi.buffalo.edu/) for  high-throughput crystallization trials.  The results of theses trials are returned to the NESG crystallization group which follows up on promising 'crystal hits'.

name: Crystal Set-Up
text: Protein crystallization set up. ******************************************  Protein is concentrated to approximately 10mg/ml using Amicon centrifugal ultra-flitration device. Use the largest molecular weight cut off that is possible to avoid co-concentration of detergent. Also, stop the runs every 5 minutes and mix in the concentrator to avoid local concentration gradient problems.  Clarify the protein prior to set up with a centrifugal filtration device (0.2um).  Store protein on ice until use.  Set up 100nl+100nl drops using the HoneyBee or Mosquito robot and Axigen plates (80ul mother liquor). Seal the plates and store in the Peltier cooled incubators at the desired temperature.  Look for xtals and record results at will.  Crystal screen solutions are purchased from Qiagen.

name: uva_crystallization_1
text: Targets are first screened in commercially available crystallization screens, usually Hampton Research's Crystal Screen I and PEG/Ion screens, using hanging-drop vapor diffusion, usually in Nextal 24-well crystallization plates. Promising hits from the initial screens are optimized by grid variation of various crystallization parameters. Microseeding is also attempted where applicable. When proteins produce crystalline hits, Se-Met derivatives of the target are produced. The Se derivatives are also screened in the commercial screens and hits from the native optimization are repeated.

name: Crystallomics_crystallization_01
text: Initial screening of crystallization conditions:  The protein samples will be screened against 384 reagent mixtures made up from 7 commercial sparse matrix screens: Crystal Screen (conditions #25 and #27 were removed), MemFac, PEG Ion, Crystal Screen Cryo, Crystal Screen II (Hampton Research), Wizard I and II (Dedode Genetics) and the locally developed SECSG MP1 screen  containing 48 conditions. Initial screening will be carried out by the sitting drop vapor diffusion method with Greiner Crystalquick plates setup by a Cartesian Honeybee crystallization robot (Genomic Solutions).  Drop composition consists of 200 nL protein solution plus 200 nL reservoir solution giving a total drop volume of 400 nL.  Once a plate has been setup, it is moved to the CrystalFarm incubator (Discovery Partners International) for storage, imaging and scoring.  Crystals are scored as follows: (1) clear, (2) precipitate, (3) crystal and (4) harvestable.  Images and scores are currently recorded in the CrystalFarm database and transferred to the Crystal Monitor (Decode Genetics) database application.  The initial screening will be carried out at two temperatures, 4 and 18oC. text: SeMet protein was expressed in E. coli in High-Yield medium with SeMet buffer (Orion Enterprises, Inc, Northbrook, IL) at 22 deg C and purified using a nickel chelating column, followed by ULP1 protease cleavage of the SUMO (Smt3) fusion, a second nickel affinity column to remove the SUMO, and a Superdex 75 size exclusion column. The protein starts with a Ser-Leu vector artifact (following SUMO cleavage) followed by residues 307-542 (UniProt Q57623); the Leu artifact matches wildtype L306, so the effective sequence is Ser-306-542. An average of 24 mg of purified SeMet protein was obtained per liter of culture. The purity and Se incorporation were assayed by SDS-PAGE analysis and mass spectrometry (ESI and MALDI), respectively. The molecular weight of the SeMet-labeled protein was 27175 Da. The purified protein was concentrated to 9 mg/ml in buffer containing 10mM HEPES pH 7.5, 150mM NaCl, 10% glycerol and 1mM b-mercaptoethanol or 5mM dithiothreitol. Crystals were obtained in 100mM sodium MES pH 7.0 and 40% MPD, mixed with protein at 1uL: 1uL protein: precipitant ratio and equilibrated by vapor diffusion against 100 uL of precipitant at room temperature.
